blind_spots.blind_spot: Fuse AI 'easily integrates with smartphones, radios, extending to weapons, drones, ground vehicles' — listed as a plug-and-play feature
blind_spots.operator_reality: Wiring a location-intelligence payload into a weapon or drone platform is squarely export-controlled technical data; the company's own materials never mention ITAR, and a Phase II contract can stall hard once the integration partner's compliance office asks the question the marketing page never answers.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The integration list is framed as a capability breadth flex, not a controlled-technology boundary.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Easily integrates with smartphones, radios, extending to weapons, drones, ground vehicles

blind_spots.blind_spot: COSINE is described as a 'Software-As-A-Service' platform, and Fuse AI 'feeds a continuous stream of raw data through our cloud-based AI system'
blind_spots.operator_reality: A cloud-round-trip inference loop directly contradicts the company's own defense pitch of working in 'low RF signal power (tree canopy, buildings, storage containers)' — exactly the DDIL conditions where a persistent cloud dependency breaks first, and nothing in the materials explains an offline/edge fallback mode.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The SaaS architecture was likely built for the commercial pilots (DFW Airport, Mohegan Sun) where connectivity is a given, then extended to the DoD narrative without re-architecting for denied comms.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Fuse AI™ feeds a continuous stream of raw data through our cloud-based AI system to enable 3D positioning, navigational context, and spatial awareness.

blind_spots.blind_spot: The DoD case study lists 'Technical Challenges' around calibration and platform integration but says nothing about who trains the soldier, what happens when the device fails mid-mission, or spares/battery logistics
blind_spots.operator_reality: Operators loving the demo isn't adoption — a fielded location system with no documented training or field-sustainment plan is exactly the kind of program that dies quietly once the SBIR funding clock runs out and the unit that piloted it moves on.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The case study is written to show quantified wins (sub-meter accuracy, better availability) rather than the operational logistics of keeping it running after handoff.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Uncertain operational environments for various use cases ranging from seen to completely unseen and dynamic environments (Training Exercises, Tactical Operations in Adversarial environments)

opener_hook: Your DoD case study cites sub-meter accuracy in GPS-contested regions — does the cloud-based inference loop hold that accuracy when the RF link itself is degraded, not just GPS?
what_they_do: Fuse AI, a software-only multi-sensor AI platform delivering real-time 3D positioning in GPS-denied/contested environments, sold to military, security/operational, and commercial navigation customers.
